protocol.name: zlm_shell_v1
protocol.copyright:
Copyright © 2026 Lumen Project SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
Private desktop environment protocol for the Lumen compositor.
PRIVILEGE MODEL (enforced by compositor, not wire-visible): - Client UID must match compositor session UID (SO_PEERCRED). - Client binary must match configured shell path (default: lumen-shell). - Optional Flatpak build: valid portal capability token required.
Regular application clients never receive the zlm_shell_v1 global.

interface.name: zlm_toplevel_v1

description.summary: compositor-owned handle for a mapped xdg toplevel

interface.description: Shell uses this object for all window management. The compositor maps zlm_toplevel_v1 to internal xdg_toplevel state. Never expose client-side xdg_toplevel references to the shell.

description.summary: destroy shell reference (does not close window)
compositor capability flags sent on bind

request.name: request_logout
request.description: The user asked to log out. The compositor sends xdg_toplevel.close to every window so clients can exit on their own terms, waits a few seconds for them to go, then stops; its teardown restores the console. Nothing is killed: a client still connected at the deadline is disconnected when the compositor exits. Repeated requests while a logout is in progress are ignored.

event.name: session_ending

description.summary: the session is about to end

event.description: A logout has begun, whoever asked for it (this shell, or the compositor's own Ctrl+Alt+Backspace). Windows are being asked to close; the connection will be closed when the compositor stops. A shell can treat that as a normal end.

request.name: grab_key

description.summary: take a key combination before any client sees it

request.description:
Creates a key grab. While it exists, a press of the combination is not sent to the focused client but reported to the shell as zlm_key_grab_v1.activated; the key's release reaches no client either. With the tap flag the grab describes a modifier key pressed and released alone, and is observed rather than taken: the key still reaches the focused client, and activated is sent on its release when no other key, pointer button or scroll happened while it was held.
keysym is an xkb keysym as the key produces it at its first shift level, in the active layout or, when that layout has no key producing it, in the first layout (so a Latin binding works under a non-Latin layout). modifiers lists exactly the modifiers that must be held; Caps Lock and Num Lock are ignored. For a tap grab keysym must be a modifier keysym and modifiers must be 0.
Grabs are not delivered during an interactive move, resize or drag, nor while the session is inactive or locked (lock_state other than unlocked). From version 6, while the focused window inhibits shortcuts (keyboard-shortcuts-inhibit-unstable-v1: a virtual machine or remote desktop viewer) its keys reach it and grabs are not delivered either, except those created with the not_inhibitable flag (the shell's lock key). A combination the compositor keeps for itself (Ctrl+Alt+ BackSpace, the XF86Switch_VT_* keysyms) or one another grab already holds is refused: the new object receives refused and stays inert until destroyed.

entry.name: locking
entry.summary: a locker asked; normal content is no longer interactive

entry.name: abandoned
entry.summary: locked, and the locker is gone: start a new one

event.name: lock_state
event.description: The ext-session-lock-v1 state of the session. Sent on bind and on every change. While it is not unlocked no shell surface is shown and none receives input, and key grabs are not delivered: the compositor guarantees this, the shell need not. On locking the shell should drop transient UI (an open launcher). On abandoned the session stays locked on a solid colour until a new locker takes over: a shell that has a lock command starts it again. The compositor's own keyboard ways out (VT switching, the logout chord) keep working while locked; logging out ends the session without revealing it.

entry.name: logind
entry.summary: loginctl lock-session, or the system asked

entry.name: sleep
entry.summary: the system is about to sleep

event.name: lock_requested
event.description: Something other than the shell asked for the session to be locked: logind's Lock signal (loginctl lock-session, a lid policy), or the system is about to sleep (the compositor holds a sleep delay until the session is locked, at most two seconds). The shell starts its locker if it has one configured; the compositor itself ships none. Not sent while the session is already locked.

event.name: capture_state
event.description: Whether some client other than this shell is capturing the screen or a window (ext-image-copy-capture-v1, wlr-screencopy): active is 1 while any such capture session delivered a frame in the last two seconds, else 0. Sent on bind and on every change. The shell shows a privacy indicator while it is 1.

interface.name: zlm_key_grab_v1

description.summary: a key combination held by the shell

interface.description: Created by zlm_shell_v1.grab_key. Destroying it gives the combination back to clients.

entry.name: tap
entry.summary: a modifier pressed and released alone

entry.name: not_inhibitable
entry.summary: the grab also fires while a client inhibits shortcuts

entry.name: invalid
entry.summary: unknown modifier or flag bits, or a tap grab on a non-modifier keysym

event.name: activated

description.summary: the combination was pressed (or the modifier tapped)

event.description: serial is an input serial delivered to this client: it may be used with xdg_activation_token_v1.set_serial (and xdg_popup.grab) as the triggering event. time is the key event's timestamp in milliseconds, as in wl_keyboard.key.

description.summary: destroy workspace; fails if not empty

interface.name: zlm_policy_bridge_v1
interface.description: Shell sends placement intent; compositor executes geometry, focus, and stacking. Stacking is default; tiling is an optional shell plugin. On bind the compositor sends a snapshot_* event batch, then delta events.

request.name: set_toplevel_stacking_index
request.description: Send multiple requests to define full order. Compositor emits stacking_order_changed with done=1 after the last index in a frame.

description.summary: start of initial state batch on bind

event.name: snapshot_toplevel

description.summary: one mapped toplevel, introducing its handle

event.description: Introduces the compositor-created handle for an already-mapped toplevel, so it is a new_id: the shell has never seen this object before. workspace is null while the compositor has no workspace objects.

event.name: toplevel_created
event.description: Followed by toplevel_state and toplevel_geometry for the same handle. workspace is null while the compositor has no workspace objects (a workspace object cannot be introduced by the compositor in this version).

event.name: toplevel_geometry
event.description: x,y,width,height is the window geometry (xdg_surface.set_window_geometry, or the whole surface when unset) in global compositor coordinates. Sent on map, on every committed size or position change, and at most once per frame during an interactive move.

description.summary: one entry in stacking order; done=1 ends batch

entry.name: not_responding
entry.summary: the client did not answer a ping in time

entry.name: demands_attention
entry.summary: an activation request was not granted focus

event.name: toplevel_flags
event.description: Sent after snapshot_toplevel and after toplevel_created when non-zero, and whenever the flags change. The compositor never acts on not_responding beyond showing it; the shell may offer to terminate the client.

event.name: toplevel_icon
event.description: The window's icon (xdg-toplevel-icon-v1) changed, or is being described in a snapshot: name is an XDG icon theme name ("" for none), followed by zero or more toplevel_icon_buffer events and toplevel_icon_done. An empty name and no buffers means the default icon (the application's desktop entry icon). Sent after snapshot_toplevel and toplevel_created when the window has an icon, and whenever it changes. The shell prefers the name, resolved in its icon theme, and falls back to the buffers.

event.name: toplevel_icon_buffer

description.summary: one pixel buffer of a toplevel's icon

event.description: fd is a sealed memfd (read-only mapping) of size x size pixels, premultiplied ARGB8888 in native byte order, stride size * 4, for the given buffer scale.

event.name: toplevel_parent
event.description: xdg_toplevel.set_parent, or a parent across clients (xdg-foreign): parent is the window this one is a dialog or child of, null for none. Sent after snapshot_toplevel and toplevel_created when there is a parent, and on change. A child in state modal blocks its parent; a task list can show the parent alone.

event.name: bell
event.description: A client rang the bell (xdg-system-bell-v1) for this window, or for no window in particular (null). The compositor limits the rate per client and drops bells while the session is locked. The shell gives feedback, e.g. a visual flash.

interface.name: zlm_window_rules_v1
interface.description: Rules are stored in the session config directory ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lumen/window-rules.toml). Use reload_rules to apply.

description.summary: reload rules from session config directory
